mainTopic: Why אסכרה comes into the world, and the story of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי's years in the cave and what followed.
overview: The amud opens with reasons why the deadly throat disease אסכרה comes into the world. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says it comes because of לשון הרע, and the גמרא asks whether that is the only cause or one cause among others. A ברייתא from the vineyard of יבנה shows that he also blamed eating untithed food, so the גמרא concludes that לשון הרע is an additional cause. In that ברייתא, רבי שמעון blames ביטול תורה and defends his view against several challenges. The last challenge is answered with the idea that innocent school children can suffer for the sins of their generation. The גמרא then explains why רבי יהודה was called ״ראש המדברים״: he praised the Roman government, while רבי שמעון בן יוחאי criticized it and was sentenced to death. This opens the famous story of רבי שמעון and his son hiding in a cave for twelve years. When they come out, they are too harsh on the world, until an old man honoring שבת shows them how much ordinary Jews love מצוות. After being reunited with his son-in-law רבי פנחס בן יאיר, רבי שמעון decides to fix something for the public, as יעקב did. He is told about a place of ספק טומאה, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another opinion: the disease comes because of slander
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the end of the view that אסכרה comes because of מעשר. Then רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says it comes because of לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: [אסכרה comes] because of tithes. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says: because of slander.
steps.whatsHappening: The first two words finish the previous opinion: the disease comes because people fail to separate מעשר. Then רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי gives his own reason: לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are in the middle of a list of sins that bring אסכרה, a disease that kills by choking the throat. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי links it to a sin of the mouth, which fits a disease that ends in the mouth. The rest of this passage will ask whether he meant this is the ONLY cause.

keyTerms.meaning: A deadly disease of the throat and mouth, similar to diphtheria
Tithes, the portion of produce that must be separated and given away

steps.confusionAlert: The words עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר are not a new statement. They finish a sentence that started on the previous page, which said אסכרה comes because of tithes.

phrases.english: for (neglecting) tithes.
phrases.notes: End of the previous opinion, which began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei says:
for slander.
phrases.notes: That is, אסכרה comes as a punishment for slander.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of causes of אסכרה from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, אסכרה comes because of לשון הרע.

steps.title: A verse hinting that liars' mouths will be stopped
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רבי יהושע בן לוי, brings a פסוק in תהלים that supports רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי: What is the verse? 'But the king shall rejoice in God; everyone who swears by Him shall glory; for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be stopped.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a פסוק as a source for the idea that people who speak falsely are punished in the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase יִסָּכֵר פִּי, 'the mouth shall be stopped,' sounds like אַסְכָּרָה and describes a mouth being closed. So the פסוק hints that sinful speech is punished by a disease that shuts the mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asks for the scriptural source)
And some say (introduces a second possible author of the statement)
Will be stopped up or closed, related in sound to אַסְכָּרָה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
What is the verse?
'But the king shall rejoice in God;
everyone who swears by Him shall glory;
for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be stopped.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural hint for רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's view.
steps.raayaObject: The link between לשון הרע and אסכרה

steps.title: Did he mean only slander, or slander as well?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי holds that לשון הרע is the only cause of אסכרה, or one more cause in addition to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Did רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי say it comes only for slander, or perhaps he said it comes also for slander?
steps.whatsHappening: The study hall raises a question about how to understand רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי. Is he disagreeing with the מעשר opinion, or adding to it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words could mean 'not for מעשר but for לשון הרע,' which is a disagreement. They could also mean 'for לשון הרע too,' which is an addition. The answer tells us whether the two views argue or can both be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; a real question raised in the study hall

phrases.english: They asked:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei,
did he say for slander (only),

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא אַף עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע נָמֵי קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: or perhaps he said also for slander?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of the statement in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether לשון הרע is the exclusive cause of אסכרה in רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's view, or an additional cause.

steps.title: Setting up the story in the vineyard of Yavne
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a ברייתא. In the vineyard of יבנה, three Sages are asked why אסכרה begins in the intestines and ends in the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When our Sages entered the vineyard in Yavne, רבי יהודה, רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, and רבי שמעון were there. This question was asked before them: Why does this plague begin in the intestines and end in the mouth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof. It introduces a ברייתא in which רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי himself will give a reason for the disease.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof will come from comparing what רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says here with what he said in step 1. The question focuses on how the disease moves through the body, from the inside up to the mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source brought as proof
The vineyard in Yavne, the place where the Sages gathered to learn

phrases.english: Come and hear:
When our Sages entered the vineyard in Yavne,
Rabbi Yehuda was there,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Shimon.
This question was asked before them:
This plague, for what reason
does it begin in the intestines and end in the mouth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that will answer the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The scope of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the vineyard in יבנה

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the mouth completes the speech
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that speech is planned inside the body but finished by the mouth, so the disease follows the same path.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי, the head of the speakers everywhere, answered and said: Even though the kidneys advise, the heart understands, and the tongue shapes the words, the mouth completes them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the first answer. Speech starts inside the body and comes out through the mouth, and the disease travels the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer fits לשון הרע. Evil speech starts as a thought inside the body and is finished by the mouth, so the punishment follows the same path. This matches רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's reason in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Kidneys, seen as the source of advice and thought

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ila'i responded,
'the head of the speakers in every place,' and said:
phrases.notes: A title of honor for רבי יהודה, who usually speaks first.

phrases.english: Even though the kidneys advise,
and the heart understands, and the tongue shapes,
the mouth completes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question asked in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disease follows the path of speech, from inside the body to the mouth, which hints at sins of speech.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: because people eat impure things
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says the disease ends in the mouth because people eat forbidden things with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי answered and said: Because people eat impure things with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, the same Sage from our question, gives his reason. It is about food, not about speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key to the proof. Here he names a cause connected to eating, not to לשון הרע. The גמרא will first fix the wording of his answer.

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei responded and said:
Because they eat non-kosher things with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer in the ברייתא, from the Sage whose view we are investigating.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mouth is punished because it eats forbidden food.

steps.title: Can it really mean non-kosher food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: would so many people really be eating non-kosher food?
steps.simpleTranslation: Impure things? Can that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the plain meaning of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A common disease cannot be blamed on a rare sin. Few Jews eat truly non-kosher food, so the words must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (a challenge that rejects an obvious reading)

phrases.english: Non-kosher things, does it enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase דברים טמאין in רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating non-kosher food is too rare to explain a widespread disease.

steps.title: It means untithed food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the words: they mean food that was not properly tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: because people eat with it things that were not properly prepared, that is, untithed food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading. 'Impure things' really means food from which מעשר was not taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's reason in the ברייתא matches the מעשר opinion from step 1. So in the ברייתא he blames untithed food, while in step 1 he blamed לשון הרע.

phrases.english: Rather, that they eat with it
things that are not properly prepared (untithed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: because of neglecting Torah study
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the disease comes because people neglect learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון answered and said: Because of the sin of neglecting Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The third Sage, רבי שמעון, gives his reason, ביטול תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mouth was meant to speak words of תורה. When it does not, it is punished. The next steps will test whether this reason holds up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon responded and said:
For the sin of neglecting Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disease comes because of ביטול תורה.

steps.title: Challenge: women get the disease too
steps.stepSummary: The Sages object that women are not obligated to learn תורה, yet they also get אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Women will prove [otherwise]!
steps.whatsHappening: The other Sages challenge רבי שמעון's reason with a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the disease comes only for ביטול תורה, people who have no obligation to learn should not get it. Women do get it, so the reason seems wrong.

phrases.english: They said to him: Women will prove (otherwise)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that the cause is ביטול תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women are not obligated to learn תורה, yet they suffer from אסכרה.

steps.title: Answer: they keep their husbands from learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that women cause their husbands to neglect תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they keep their husbands from learning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends his reason. Women are punished for causing others to neglect תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He widens ביטול תורה to include making someone else stop learning. This keeps his reason true even for people who are not obligated themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Cause others to be idle from learning

phrases.english: Because they cause their husbands to be idle (from Torah).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening the definition of the sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only people who fail to learn themselves are guilty of ביטול תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Causing someone else to neglect learning also counts.

steps.title: Challenge: non-Jews get the disease too
steps.stepSummary: The Sages object that non-Jews are not obligated in תורה, yet they also get אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Non-Jews will prove [otherwise]!
steps.whatsHappening: A second counterexample is raised against רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jews have no obligation to learn תורה at all. If they get the disease, ביטול תורה cannot be its cause.

phrases.english: Gentiles will prove (otherwise)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, following the defense in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Non-Jews are not obligated in תורה, yet they get אסכרה.

steps.title: Answer: they keep Jews from learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that non-Jews cause the Jewish people to neglect תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they keep the Jewish people from learning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון uses the same kind of answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jews who oppress or distract Jews take them away from learning. So they too are guilty of causing ביטול תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Cause the Jewish people to stop learning

phrases.english: Because they cause Israel to be idle (from Torah).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Non-Jews have no connection to ביטול תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They cause Jews to neglect learning.

steps.title: Challenge: young children get the disease too
steps.stepSummary: The Sages object that little children are not obligated to learn, yet they get אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Children will prove [otherwise]!
steps.whatsHappening: A third counterexample is raised against רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Young children are not obligated in מצוות at all. So why would they be punished for ביטול תורה?

phrases.english: Children will prove (otherwise)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Young children have no obligation, yet they get the disease.

steps.title: Answer: they keep their fathers from learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that children distract their fathers from learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they keep their fathers from learning.
steps.whatsHappening: Again, רבי שמעון answers that the children cause someone else to neglect תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Caring for children takes fathers away from their learning. This is the same pattern as the last two answers.

phrases.english: Because they cause their fathers to be idle (from Torah).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Children have no connection to ביטול תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They cause their fathers to neglect learning.

steps.title: Challenge: school children who learn get it too
steps.stepSummary: The final challenge: school children are actively learning תורה, yet they also get אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: School children will prove [otherwise]!
steps.whatsHappening: The strongest challenge is raised. The ברייתא itself gives no answer, but the גמרא answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: School children are learning תורה, so the 'causing others to neglect' answer cannot work for them. רבי שמעון's pattern of answers breaks down here.

keyTerms.meaning: School children who learn Torah with a teacher

phrases.english: School children will prove (otherwise)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final challenge. The ברייתא does not answer it; the גמרא answers it in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These children are learning, not neglecting תורה, yet they suffer.

steps.title: Innocent children may suffer for the generation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבי גוריון's teaching: when there are no צדיקים in the generation, school children suffer for the generation's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it follows רבי גוריון. רבי גוריון said, and some say רב יוסף ברבי שמעיה: When there are righteous people in the generation, the righteous are seized for the generation. When there are no righteous people in the generation, school children are seized for the generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself answers the last challenge. The school children do not suffer for their own sin. They suffer for the sins of others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רבי שמעון's reason intact. The disease still comes because of sin, but sometimes innocent people carry the punishment for the whole generation.

keyTerms.meaning: Are seized, punished in place of others

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the school children did something wrong. The point is the opposite: they are innocent and suffer for the sins of others.

phrases.english: There, it is in accordance with Rabbi Guryon,
as Rabbi Guryon said,
and some say Rav Yosef son of Rabbi Shemaya:
At a time when there are righteous people in the generation,
the righteous are seized for the generation.
When there are no righteous people in the generation,

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן נִתְפָּסִים עַל הַדּוֹר.
phrases.english: school children are seized for the generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unanswered challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: suffering for others rather than for one's own sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: School children suffer for their own ביטול תורה, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are innocent and suffer for the sins of the generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key idea in the גמרא: the suffering of innocent people can come from the sins of the community around them.

steps.title: A verse: young goats taken as a pledge for the shepherds
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in שיר השירים is brought as the source for רבי גוריון's idea. The young goats are taken as collateral for the shepherds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר זעירי said, and some say רבי שמעון בן נזירא said: What is the verse? 'If you do not know, fairest among women, go forth in the footsteps of the flock...' And we explain: the young goats are taken as collateral for the shepherds.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a פסוק to support the idea that children suffer for their leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse continues 'feed your kids by the shepherds' tents (מִשְׁכְּנוֹת).' The גמרא reads מִשְׁכְּנוֹת as 'collateral' (מַשְׁכּוֹן). So the young, the 'kids,' are taken as a pledge for the sins of the shepherds, the leaders.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
And we say (we explain the verse)
Taken as collateral, held as a pledge
Shepherds, representing the leaders of the generation

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ze'iri said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נְזִירָא:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Nezira said:
What is the verse?
'If you do not know, fairest among women,
go forth in the footsteps of the flock, etc.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:8; the verse continues 'and feed your kids by the shepherds' tents.'

phrases.english: And we say:
young goats that are taken as collateral for the shepherds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for רבי גוריון's teaching in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that children suffer for the sins of their leaders
steps.raayaSupportSource: Song of Songs 1:8, read with מִשְׁכְּנוֹת as 'collateral'

steps.title: Conclusion: slander is also a cause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי meant לשון הרע is ALSO a cause of אסכרה, not the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: he said it comes also for slander. Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its question from step 3 and answers it, using the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי blamed untithed food, and earlier he blamed לשון הרע. So he must hold that both are causes. לשון הרע is an additional cause, not the only one.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי holds that אסכרה comes from more than one sin: לשון הרע and also eating untithed food. The proof is that in the ברייתא of יבנה he gives the untithed-food reason.

phrases.english: Conclude from it:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע נָמֵי קָאָמַר —
phrases.english: he said also for slander.
Indeed, conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of step 3 and resolves it from the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, לשון הרע is an additional cause of אסכרה, alongside eating untithed food.

steps.title: Why was רבי יהודה called the head of the speakers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה's title ״ראש המדברים בכל מקום״ came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call him "the head of the speakers in every place"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a background question about a title given to רבי יהודה. This question sets up a long story that will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier ברייתא described רבי יהודה as ״ראש המדברים בכל מקום״, the first to speak everywhere. The גמרא is not challenging anything. It simply wants to know the origin of this honor, and the answer will turn into a long narrative.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the speakers; the one who always speaks first

phrases.english: And why did they call him
"head of the speakers in every place"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts away from the topic of אסכרה to explain a title mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The origin of רבי יהודה's title ״ראש המדברים בכל מקום״.

steps.title: The scene: רבי יהודה praises the Romans
steps.stepSummary: Three תנאים sit together with יהודה בן גרים nearby, and רבי יהודה praises what the Romans built.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון were sitting, and יהודה בן גרים sat with them. רבי יהודה began: How nice are the deeds of this nation. They built markets, bridges and bathhouses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by setting the scene. רבי יהודה opens the conversation with praise for the Roman government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay attention to the detail that יהודה בן גרים is sitting nearby. He is the one who will later repeat the conversation. רבי יהודה's positive words about Rome are what will eventually earn him his title.

keyTerms.meaning: Yehuda, son of converts; the listener who later repeats the conversation

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda was sitting
with Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon,
and Yehuda son of converts sat beside them.
Rabbi Yehuda opened and said:

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה נָאִים מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל אוּמָּה זוֹ:
phrases.english: How pleasant are the deeds of this nation:
they established markets, they established bridges,
they established bathhouses.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיָתְבִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The opening of the story: רבי יהודה praised the Romans in front of יהודה בן גרים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי is silent and רבי שמעון criticizes Rome
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says nothing. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי argues that every Roman project was built only for selfish reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי was silent. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answered: Everything they built, they built only for themselves. Markets, to put prostitutes in them. Bathhouses, to pamper themselves. Bridges, to collect tolls.
steps.whatsHappening: The other two תנאים react to רבי יהודה's praise. רבי יוסי stays quiet, and רבי שמעון rejects the praise point by point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון goes through the same three projects and gives each one a selfish motive. Now each of the three sages has taken a different position: praise, silence, and criticism. Each position will receive a matching consequence.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei was silent.

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai responded and said:
Everything that they established,
they established only for their own purposes.
They established markets, to place prostitutes in them;
bathhouses, to pamper themselves in them;
bridges, to collect tolls from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reactions of the other two sages to רבי יהודה's praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון holds that Rome's public works were built only for selfish purposes.

steps.title: The government rewards and punishes each sage
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בן גרים repeats the conversation, and Rome decides: רבי יהודה is promoted, רבי יוסי is exiled, and רבי שמעון is sentenced to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בן גרים went and repeated their words, and they reached the government. They said: יהודה, who praised us, will be raised up. יוסי, who was silent, will be exiled to ציפורי. שמעון, who criticized us, will be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual answer to the question. Because רבי יהודה praised Rome, the government made him ״ראש המדברים״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each consequence matches what the sage said: praise brings promotion, silence brings exile, and criticism brings death. The phrase ״יתעלה״, meaning "will be raised up", is the appointment that gave רבי יהודה his title.
steps.confusionAlert: יהודה בן גרים is a different person from רבי יהודה. Do not mix up the one who repeated the conversation with the sage who praised Rome.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the question from step 20 and opens the famous story of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי in hiding.

phrases.english: Yehuda son of converts went
and related their words,
and they were heard by the government.
They said: Yehuda, who elevated us, shall be elevated.
Yosei, who was silent, shall be exiled to Tzippori.
Shimon, who denounced us, shall be killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ יְהוּדָה בֶּן גֵּרִים וְסִיפֵּר דִּבְרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the outcome of the conversation, which answers the question about the title.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה was appointed by Rome (״יתעלה״) because he praised them, and that is how he became ״ראש המדברים״.

steps.title: Hiding in the בית מדרש, then moving to a cave
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון and his son hide in the בית מדרש, where his wife feeds them. When the danger grows, they move to a cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He and his son went and hid in the study hall. Every day his wife brought them bread and a jug of water, and they ate. When the decree grew stronger, he told his son: Women are easily pressured. Maybe they will torture her and she will reveal where we are. So they went and hid in a cave.
steps.whatsHappening: The story now follows רבי שמעון after the death sentence. He hides with his son, and then moves to a safer place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the wife brings food, the plan depends on her. Once the decree becomes harsher, רבי שמעון worries she could be tortured into revealing them. He moves somewhere she does not know about, both to protect her and to keep them safe.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל הוּא וּבְרֵיהּ, טְשׁוֹ בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: He and his son went and hid in the study hall.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה מַתְיָא לְהוּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ
phrases.english: Every day his wife would bring them
bread and a jug of water, and they would eat.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תְּקֵיף גְּזֵירְתָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: When the decree intensified, he said to his son:
Women are easily pressured;
perhaps they will torture her and she will reveal us.
They went and hid in a cave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל הוּא וּבְרֵיהּ, טְשׁוֹ בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי שמעון's death sentence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון and his son hide, first in the בית מדרש and then in a cave.

steps.title: Twelve years of miracles and learning in the cave
steps.stepSummary: A carob tree and a spring miraculously appear. They learn all day buried in sand, and after twelve years אליהו הנביא announces that the decree has ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: A miracle happened: a carob tree and a spring of water were created for them. They took off their clothes and sat in sand up to their necks, learning all day. At prayer time they got dressed, covered themselves and prayed, then took their clothes off again so they would not wear out. They stayed in the cave twelve years. אליהו came, stood at the cave's entrance, and said: Who will tell בר יוחאי that the emperor has died and his decree is canceled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how they survived and how devoted they were to Torah during twelve years in the cave. It ends with אליהו telling them the danger is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ gives them food and water so they can survive. They save their only clothes for תפילה by sitting in sand while they learn. Twelve years of total Torah study sets up the problem in the next step, when they come out and judge the outside world harshly.

phrases.english: A miracle occurred:
a carob tree and a spring of water were created for them,
and they would take off their clothes
and sit in sand up to their necks.
All day they would study.
At prayer time they would dress, cover themselves, and pray,
and then they would take off their clothes again
so that they would not wear out.
They sat twelve years in the cave.
Eliyahu came and stood at the entrance of the cave,
and said: Who will inform bar Yochai
that the emperor died and his decree is canceled?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְרְחִישׁ נִיסָּא אִיבְּרִי לְהוּ חָרוּבָא וְעֵינָא דְמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes their life in the cave and the end of the danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They spent twelve years in total Torah study, supported by a miracle, until אליהו announced the decree had ended.

steps.title: Too harsh on the world: sent back to the cave
steps.stepSummary: They come out, see people farming, and burn everything they look at. A בת קול sends them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came out and saw people plowing and sowing. They said: These people leave eternal life and busy themselves with temporary life. Every place they looked at was immediately burned. A heavenly voice came out and said to them: Did you come out to destroy My world? Go back to your cave!
steps.whatsHappening: After twelve years of pure Torah, they cannot accept people working for a living, and their gaze destroys things. Heaven rejects this attitude and sends them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They see farming as abandoning Torah, which they call ״חיי עולם״, for worldly concerns, which they call ״חיי שעה״. The בת קול teaches that ה׳'s world also needs people to work it. Their harsh attitude is treated as a fault that has to be fixed.

phrases.aramaic: נְפַקוּ, חֲזוֹ אִינָשֵׁי דְּקָא כָּרְבִי וְזָרְעִי,
phrases.english: They came out and saw people plowing and sowing.
They said: They abandon eternal life
and engage in temporary life!

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין עֵינֵיהֶן מִיָּד נִשְׂרָף.
phrases.english: Every place they set their eyes was immediately burned.
A heavenly voice came out and said to them:
Did you come out to destroy My world?!
Return to your cave!

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַקוּ, חֲזוֹ אִינָשֵׁי דְּקָא כָּרְבִי וְזָרְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened when they first came out of the cave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven rejects their destructive harshness toward people earning a living.

steps.title: Twelve more months, and רבי שמעון heals what his son harms
steps.stepSummary: After twelve more months they come out again. רבי שמעון now heals whatever רבי אלעזר damages, and tells his son that the two of them are enough for the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went back and stayed twelve months. They said: The punishment of the wicked in גיהנם is twelve months. A heavenly voice came out and said: Leave your cave! They came out. Wherever רבי אלעזר would strike, רבי שמעון would heal. He said to him: My son, you and I are enough for the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Their extra time in the cave is over and they come out a second time. רבי שמעון has softened, but his son רבי אלעזר is still harsh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twelve months matches the longest punishment in גיהנם, so they feel their sin has been forgiven. רבי שמעון now repairs the damage instead of causing it. He calms his son by saying that the two of them learning is enough for the world, so there is no need to be angry at others.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place where souls are punished

phrases.aramaic: הֲדוּר אֲזוּל אִיתִּיבוּ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא.
phrases.english: They went back and sat twelve months of a year.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: מִשְׁפַּט רְשָׁעִים בְּגֵיהִנָּם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: They said: The judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom is twelve months.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה: צְאוּ מִמְּעָרַתְכֶם!
phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said: Leave your cave!
They came out.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הֵיכָא דַּהֲוָה מָחֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Wherever Rabbi Elazar would strike,
Rabbi Shimon would heal.
He said to him: My son,
you and I are enough for the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדוּר אֲזוּל אִיתִּיבוּ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes their second time coming out of the cave and רבי שמעון's change of attitude.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון now repairs the harm instead of causing it, though רבי אלעזר is still not fully calmed.

steps.title: The old man with two bundles of myrtle for שבת
steps.stepSummary: Right before שבת, they see an old man running with two bundles of myrtle. He explains they correspond to ״זכור״ and ״שמור״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just before שבת came in, they saw an old man holding two bundles of myrtle and running at twilight. They asked him: What are these for? He said: In honor of שבת. They asked: Wouldn't one be enough? He answered: One is for ״זכור״ (Remember) and one is for ״שמור״ (Observe).
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows them an ordinary Jew going out of his way for a מצוה. This scene sets up the final lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one bundle would honor שבת, but the old man brings two, one for each wording of the commandment. The two wordings are ״זכור״ in the עשרת הדברות of ספר שמות and ״שמור״ in the repetition in ספר דברים. This shows that simple working people also love מצוות deeply.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב שבת, the eve of שבת

phrases.english: Toward evening on Shabbat eve,
they saw a certain old man
who was holding two bundles of myrtle
and running at twilight.
They said to him: Why do you have these?
He said to them: In honor of Shabbat.
They said: Let one be enough for you!
He answered: One corresponds to "Remember" and one to "Observe."

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּהֲדֵי פַּנְיָא דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא חֲזוֹ הָהוּא סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the scene that will finally calm רבי שמעון and his son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary Jew honors שבת with two bundles, one for ״זכור״ and one for ״שמור״.

steps.title: See how beloved the מצוות are: their minds are put at ease
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון tells his son to see how much Jews love מצוות, and they are finally at peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his son: See how beloved the מצוות are to the Jewish people. And their minds were put at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of this part of the story. Seeing the old man, רבי שמעון and his son finally make peace with ordinary Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their problem was thinking that people who work are abandoning ״חיי עולם״. The old man shows that working people treasure מצוות too. Once they see this, their anger at the world is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Their minds were put at ease

steps.whatToRemember: The story moves from harshness to acceptance. רבי שמעון first burns the world, then heals it, and finally learns to appreciate ordinary Jews' love of מצוות through the old man with the two myrtle bundles.

phrases.english: He said to his son:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזִי כַּמָּה חֲבִיבִין מִצְוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: See how beloved the מצוות are to Israel.
Their minds were put at ease.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזִי כַּמָּה חֲבִיבִין מִצְוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the old man's actions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Ordinary Jews' love for מצוות shows their worth, and רבי שמעון and his son are finally at peace with the world.

steps.title: רבי פנחס בן יאיר sees the damage on רבי שמעון's body
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר goes out to greet his father-in-law and brings him to the bathhouse. He sees cracks in his skin and cries, and his tears sting רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פנחס בן יאיר, his son-in-law, heard and went out to greet him. He brought him into the bathhouse and was caring for his skin. He saw that there were cracks in his body. He cried, and his tears fell and caused רבי שמעון pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי פנחס בן יאיר hears that his father-in-law רבי שמעון is out of the cave and takes care of him in the bathhouse. He sees the painful results of twelve years buried in sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cracks in his skin come from sitting in sand for years, as described in the earlier steps. The tears even hurt רבי שמעון because his skin is so raw. This sets up the conversation in the next step about what that suffering means.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר חַתְנֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, his son-in-law, heard
and went out to greet him.
He brought him into the bathhouse,
and was tending to his flesh.
He saw that there were cracks in his body.
phrases.notes: From years of being buried in sand in the cave.

phrases.english: He was crying
and the tears were falling from his eyes
and they caused him (Rabbi Shimon) pain.
phrases.notes: The salty tears stung the open cracks.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר חַתְנֵיהּ וּנְפַק לְאַפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רבי שמעון and his son finally leave the cave at peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: רבי פנחס בן יאיר sees the physical cost of the years in the cave and weeps.

steps.title: Woe is me versus happy are you
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר says, 'Woe is me that I see you like this.' רבי שמעון answers, 'Happy are you that you see me like this, because otherwise you would not find this greatness in me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Woe is me that I have seen you like this. He answered: Happy are you that you have seen me like this, because if you had not seen me like this, you would not have found in me this (greatness in Torah).
steps.whatsHappening: The two have a short exchange: the son-in-law mourns the suffering, and רבי שמעון turns it into something positive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פנחס sees only the pain. רבי שמעון explains that the years of suffering and learning in the cave are what built his Torah greatness, so the pain was worth it. The word 'כך' (this) at the end means his level of Torah, which the next step proves.

keyTerms.meaning: Happy are you / fortunate are you
Had it not been that / if not for

steps.confusionAlert: Both phrases use 'בכך' and 'כך', but they mean different things. 'רְאִיתַנִי בְּכָךְ' means 'seen me in this condition' (the cracks). 'מָצָאתָ בִּי כָּךְ' means 'found in me this greatness' (Torah).

phrases.english: He said to him: Woe is me
that I have seen you like this.
He said to him: Happy are you
that you have seen me like this,
because had you not seen me like this,
you would not have found this in me.
phrases.notes: 'This' refers to his greatness in Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹי לִי שֶׁרְאִיתִיךָ בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the crying in the previous step by giving the suffering a meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suffering for Torah is what produced רבי שמעון's greatness in Torah.

steps.title: From twelve answers to twenty-four answers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how much רבי שמעון grew. Before the cave, רבי פנחס could answer his questions with twelve answers. After the cave, רבי שמעון could answer רבי פנחס's questions with twenty-four answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, when רבי שמעון בן יוחי asked a difficult question, רבי פנחס בן יאיר would give him twelve answers. In the end, when רבי פנחס בן יאיר asked a difficult question, רבי שמעון בן יוחי would give him twenty-four answers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי שמעון's claim from the previous step by showing how much his learning grew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the cave, רבי פנחס was the stronger one: he answered רבי שמעון's questions. After the cave, the roles flipped, and רבי שמעון gave twice as many answers. This shows concretely what 'you would not have found this in me' means.
steps.whatToRemember: The years of suffering in the cave doubled רבי שמעון's Torah. Before, his son-in-law רבי פנחס בן יאיר answered his questions with twelve answers. Afterward, רבי שמעון answered רבי פנחס's questions with twenty-four answers.

phrases.english: For at first, when he would ask
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, a difficult question,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְפָרֵק לֵיהּ רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
phrases.english: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair would answer him
with twelve answers.
In the end, when he would ask
Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, a difficult question,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְפָרֵק לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai would answer him
with twenty-four answers.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא כִּי הֲוָה מַקְשֵׁי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי קוּשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and illustrates רבי שמעון's claim that his suffering built his Torah.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's claim that his greatness came from the time in the cave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reversal from twelve answers given to him, to twenty-four answers given by him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון decides to repair something, like יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that since a miracle happened to him, he will go fix something for others. He bases this on יעקב, who came 'שלם' (whole) and then did something for the city. רב explains 'שלם' as whole in body, money, and Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Since a miracle happened to me, I will go and fix something. As it is written: 'And יעקב came whole.' And רב said: whole in his body, whole in his money, whole in his Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns: רבי שמעון wants to give back after being saved by a miracle, and he brings a source from יעקב אבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב was also saved from danger (from עשו and לבן) and came out 'whole.' The verse continues that he then did something for the city, which the next step explains. The lesson is that one who is saved by a miracle should do something good for the public.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea that being saved by a miracle creates a responsibility to do something good for others.

phrases.english: He said: Since a miracle happened (to me),
I will go and fix something.
As it is written: 'And Jacob came whole,'
and Rav said: whole in his body,
whole in his money, whole in his Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: הוֹאִיל וְאִיתְרְחִישׁ נִיסָּא אֵיזִיל אַתְקֵין מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the healing and reunion to what רבי שמעון will do now that he is out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who experiences a miracle should repair something for the public, as יעקב did after coming out 'שלם.'

steps.title: What יעקב fixed for the city: three opinions
steps.stepSummary: The verse continues 'and he graced the face of the city.' רב says יעקב set up coins for them, שמואל says markets, and רבי יוחנן says bathhouses.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he graced the face of the city': רב said, he set up a currency for them. שמואל said, he set up markets for them. רבי יוחנן said, he set up bathhouses for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from יעקב by explaining what good he did for the city after being saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three opinions agree that יעקב did something practical to help the people of the city; they only argue about what it was. This is the part of the verse that actually shows 'fixing something,' which is what רבי שמעון wants to copy.

keyTerms.meaning: And he graced the face of the city

phrases.english: 'And he graced the face of the city,'
Rav said: He set up a currency for them,
and Shmuel said: He set up markets for them,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת תִּיקֵּן לָהֶם.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said: He set up bathhouses for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the verse quoted in the previous step and shows the 'fixing' יעקב did.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's decision to repair something after his miracle.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יעקב 'graced the city' with currency, markets, or bathhouses after arriving 'שלם.'

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks what needs fixing
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks the people whether there is something that needs to be repaired.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Is there something that needs to be fixed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון turns his decision into action by asking the people what needs fixing. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not choose a project on his own. He asks what the community actually needs, so his help will be useful to them.

phrases.english: He said: Is there something
that needs to be fixed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the decision to 'fix something,' based on יעקב's example, into practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the town needs repair?

steps.title: The people point to a place of doubtful impurity
steps.stepSummary: The people tell רבי שמעון that there is a place with ספק טומאה, meaning it is unclear whether it is ritually impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There is a place that has a doubt of ritual impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The people answer his question: there is an area where nobody knows for sure whether there is impurity, such as a buried grave. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of this doubt, כהנים and people who want to stay ritually pure must avoid the area or walk around it. Fixing this means clarifying where the impurity actually is, which will help the whole community.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about ritual impurity (e.g., possibly a grave there)

phrases.english: They said to him: There is a place
that has a doubt of ritual impurity

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא דּוּכְתָּא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's question of what needs fixing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A place with ספק טומאה needs to be clarified.
